articleTitle: Optimal Parameter Extraction of Triple-Diode Photovoltaic Model Using Frilled Lizard Optimization
abstract: In this paper, a novel and efficient method for high accuracy parameter estimation of the three-diode solar cell model is proposed. In this regard, Newton-Raphson numerical method was integrated to increase the efficiency of the Frilled Lizard Optimisation (FLO) algorithm and the analyses were performed with reference to the RTC France module data. In addition, the root mean square error (RMSE) was selected as the objective function, and the results obtained were compared with the harris hawks optimisation, particle swarm optimisation, sine cosine algorithm, multi-verse optimisation, grey wolf optimiser, dragonfly algorithm optimisation algorithms reported in the literature in various metrics. The results obtained show that the proposed algorithm has high accuracy and strong consistency compared to other studies, especially with the lowest RMSE value of 0.0073024.

articleTitle: Numerical Model for Thermal Performance: Analysis of a Panel Radiator Cap and Ventilation Grills
abstract: In this study, a numerical model is developed to analyze the thermal behavior of a panel type (PCP) aluminum radiator used for space heating. The developed model is applied for a slice of the radiator and convection and radiation effects are included in the calculations. The effects of backside vents, radiator cap and its openings are investigated. The model accuracy tests were carried out in the test chamber located in the Thermal Sciences Laboratory of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, Gazi University, using the test results carried out according to TS EN 442 standard on the market equivalent of the analyzed radiator. The test chamber was equipped according to ANSI/ASHRAE-138 standard and converted to TS EN 442 radiator test. The results of the numerical analysis show that 600-800-1100-1400 W thermal power can be obtained for temperature differences of 30-40-50-60°C using the radiator under investigation and the heat transfer coefficient of the radiator was found to be between 5-8 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> K on average. The openings at the back of the radiator enhance the radiator power by approximately 6,7%. Radiator cap reduces the radiator power of the radiator by about 10%. The open air vent of the radiator cap increases the power by 1.4%. The effect of this is limited.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a MIMO Channel Simulator for Smart Grid Communications
abstract: 5G Communication technologies are crucial realising the potential benefits of smart grids (SG), enabling real-time communication between electric utilities, their devices and customers on the network. Massive multiple input multiple output communication (MIMO) is a key technique in 5G, enhancing energy efficiency and high data rates communication. However, it is imperative to have accurate and realistic channel models for effective MIMO communication; this complicated task is achieved using MIMO channel simulators. Thus, the MIMO simulator reproduces the statistical properties of the non-realizable reference model with sufficient accuracy while keeping complexity very low. Nevertheless, designing accurate and efficient MIMO channel simulators is often challenging. This paper examines the theoretical performance of the MIMO channel simulator in an isotropic environment using both existing and newly modified parameterisation methods. The existing methods include the Extended Method of Exact Doppler Spread (EMEDS) and the Modified Method of Equal Area (MMEA). The new improved methods are Modified Extended Method of Exact Doppler Spread (MEMEDS) and the New Modified Method of Equal Area (NMMEA). Theoretical performance evaluations of the MIMO channel simulator using this conventional and enhanced methods are investigated.

Author Keywords: Modified Extended Method of Exact Doppler Spread
New Modified Method of Equal Area

articleTitle: Design of Flexible Charging Simulator for Electric Vehicles
abstract: The widespread use of electric vehicles (EVs) has made the charging methods for their batteries a critical issue that warrants examination. Significantly, the battery part is an essential cost item in EVs. In addition to vehicle usage, charging practices also considerably affect battery life. In this study, unnecessary battery degradation has been tried to be prevented while considering the demands of vehicle users. For this purpose, a simulation model has been proposed that allows users to select battery capacity, charging current, and battery health mode based on their preferences. Battery life can be extended with more flexible charging instead of constantly wearing out the battery with stable, fast charging. In this way, a more sensitive and user-vehicle interactive charging can be performed. Due to this approach, some improvements can be observed in the degradation graph of the battery, and the aging phenomenon is reduced substantially. The simulator has been designed with the help of a general user interface (GUI) based on MATLAB/Simulink environment. This user-friendly interface design also prevents unnecessary charging and eliminates unwanted load shedding on the grid.

articleTitle: Dynamic Economic Load Dispatch Using GAMS
abstract: This study addresses dynamic economic load dispatch, a critical and complex problem in power systems that aims to minimize fuel costs for the efficient operation of power systems. To solve this problem, GAMS software was used, known for its high solution capability, ease of application, fast computation time, and ability to achieve optimal results in handling complex problems. The model was developed for two different test systems, consisting of 5 and 10 generating units. Constraints such as generator capacity, demand and ramp rate were incorporated into the solution. According to the analysis results, the total fuel cost for the 5-unit system was $40,121, while for the 10-unit system it was $2,422,246. The results show a clear advantage in daily fuel costs compared to methods like GA, DE-SQP, PSOSQP, and PSOCS. Specifically, the GAMS approach achieves an annual total fuel cost saving of approximately $1,460,000 for the 5-unit system and $28,400,000 for the 10-unit system.

articleTitle: Maximize the Electricity Production from PV System Employing the Optimum Tilt Angle
abstract: With the intention to optimize the amount of solar radiation that is taken in by a photovoltaic (PV) panel and, therefore, the amount of solar power that is generated, it is essential to determine the optimal tilt angle of the PV panels for a particular geographical region. Photovoltaic electricity is the fastest-growing clean power source. Solar panels have variable characteristics in relation to temperature and irradiance. Under partial shade situations, the photovoltaic array exhibits many peaks, necessitating the maximum power point method to be optimized for identifying the peak with the highest power output. Evaluating the characteristics of photovoltaic clusters under standard irradiance and partial shade is essential for optimizing power extraction from the PV array. In this work we study the effect of tilt angle of PV system to generate electrical power in three Iraqi cities (Mosul, Karbala, Basra) with various system. Also, the findings acquired will enhance the understanding, management, planning, forecasting, and stabilization of solar power production. The simulation outcomes clarify optimal tilt angle of solar panels for 3 cities in Iraq a(Mosul- Karbala-Basra) was (33°, 30°, 29°), respectively. This work was implemented by RET screen and PVGIS software.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Time Series Prediction of Micro Gas Turbine Power Output
abstract: Micro gas turbines play an important role in energy production, and it is critical to make accurate predictions in order to ensure that these turbines operate efficiently. The objective of this study is to predict the power output of micro gas turbines using three different deep learning models (artificial neural network (ANN), convolutional neural network (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM)) based on the input voltage data. A time series approach is employed to model the impact of the input voltage on power generation. Another objective of the study is to analyze the efficacy of deep learning-based methods for predicting the power output of micro gas turbines. The results indicate that the ANN model has a MAPE value of approximately 16%, the CNN model has a value of about 26%, and the LSTM model has a value of almost 20%. The ANN model demonstrates the lowest error rate, while the LSTM and CNN models exhibit satisfactory performance. These findings indicate that time series data can be effectively used to predict the power output of micro gas turbines. It is anticipated that in the future, the approaches will be further developed and applied more widely in industry as larger data sets and more sophisticated model improvements become available.

articleTitle: Preview of 3-Phase Induction Motor Design
abstract: This paper focuses on the outline of asynchronous motor design. It is summarized which parameters change what while designing. These parameters can be used to obtain information on the main dimensions of the asynchronous motor structure. It is also shown which factors a designer should consider when designing a motor. The starting current and starting torque of a 3-phase 11 kW, 380V 6-pole 900 rpm asynchronous motor are analyzed. The effect of slot length and width on starting torque and starting current is analyzed. In addition to these, the effect of some other parameters is discussed.

articleTitle: A Novel Puma Optimizer Based TID Controller for Load Frequency Control
abstract: This paper presents the Puma Optimizer (PO) algorithm, a novel approach to the load frequency control problem. The proposed PO algorithm optimizes the gain parameters of the tilt-integral-derivative (TID) controller used for load frequency control in a two-area interconnected power system with a PV system. In this study, the proposed PO algorithm for optimizing the TID controller was compared with ImRSA, RSA, MGWO-CS and PDO algorithms, which were previously published in the literature. In the optimization of the TID controller's gain parameters based on the ITAE metric, the proposed PO algorithm achieved the best performance with a value of 0.7441, followed by ImRSA with 0.8239, RSA with 0.9251, MGWO-CS with 0.9203 and PDO with 0.8108. The performance of the optimized TID controller was evaluated based on the system's frequency response to a 0.1 p.u load disturbance in both areas. According to the simulation results obtained, it was observed that the proposed PO algorithm provided the fastest settling time and the minimum overshoot and undershoot values in the frequency response of the system in both areas and the tie-line against load changes.

articleTitle: Development of Supported Catalyst for Hydrogen Production From Sodium Borohydride
abstract: The best solution to the problems caused by fossil fuels and the limitations of renewable energy sources is the conversion of hydrogen into energy in fuel cells. The transportation and storage problems, which are the main obstacles to the conversion of hydrogen into energy in fuel cells, can be overcome by storing hydrogen in boron compounds. The recovery of hydrogen stored in boron compounds when needed is carried out through catalytic processes. In this study, a supported catalyst was synthesized for use in hydrogen production from sodium borohydride (SBH), which is one of the main boron compounds used in the solid storage of hydrogen, and the dehydrogenation parameters of the synthesized catalyst were investigated. In this context, chenopodium botrys plant extract was used as a support material for nickel (Ni) metal atoms. At the end of the extraction carried out through a hydrothermal process, Ni atoms were decorated using the impregnation method in the extract, and the Ni@KBHE catalyst was produced via reduction under SBH. After the washing, filtration, and drying processes were carried out under a nitrogen atmosphere, the solution medium, catalyst amount, SBH concentration, and temperature parameters of SBH hydrolysis with the crumbled catalyst were optimized. Optimum values for hydrogen production were obtained using 5% NaOH, 60 mg of catalyst, and 2% SBH. The hydrogen production rate (HGR) at these values was 4664 mL/g min. As a result of the catalytic reaction kinetic calculations, it was determined that the reaction was nth order, and the reaction activation energy was 49.4 kJ/mol.

articleTitle: Optimizing ML-Based Solar PV Forecasting Models in Smart Grids
abstract: In this paper, the impact of data pre-processing strategies on the performance of forecasting models for solar power generation is comprehensively analyzed. The integration of outlier detection, normalization, and missing data handling techniques with popular ML models such as XGBoost, Light-GBM, and Random Forest is investigated. The effects of six different pre-processing methods on three different ML models are examined over a total of 81 possible combinations. Two different scenarios have been used: one with a dataset without missing values (Scenario 1) and one with a dataset with missing values (Scenario 2). The results highlight that data pre-processing can significantly affect the accuracy and the importance of specific pre-processing methods in optimizing ML models for specific datasets and algorithms.

articleTitle: Strengthening Energy Infrastructure Security: A Blockchain Approach for SCADA Systems
abstract: This paper explores the potential of integrating blockchain technology to enhance security in Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems. SCADA systems are widely used in various industries to monitor and control critical infrastructure, making them prime targets for cyber attacks. By leveraging the decentralized and tamperresistant properties of blockchain, SCADA systems can be better protected against cyber threats. This research examines the benefits, challenges, and implementation strategies of incorporating blockchain-based security systems in SCADA environments. Case studies and real-world examples are analyzed to demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach. The findings of this study provide valuable insights for organizations looking to strengthen the security of their SCADA systems.

articleTitle: Core Loss Analysis in Power Transformers: A Finite Element Method Approach Considering Voltage Harmonics Impact
abstract: This study presents an investigation into the impacts of voltage harmonics on the core losses of power transformers. Both the finite element method (FEM) and the conventional method of calculating core losses using the Specific No Load Loss (SNLL) curve were applied. The core losses were analyzed under conditions of 0% Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) and 7.83% THD of voltage applied to the primary winding. The results were compared to evaluate the additional losses induced by harmonics. The findings indicate that harmonics can lead to significant extra losses in the core, resulting in temperature rise and reduced lifespan of transformers. Therefore, it is crucial to consider harmonics in the design process of transformers to ensure their reliability and longevity.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches for Predicting Power Generation in Wave Energy Converters
abstract: The potential of wave energy as a renewable energy source is significant, and therefore the development of accurate methods for predicting power output from Wave Energy Converters (WECs) is a necessity. This study employs a dataset from the UCI Machine Learning Repository. Five regression techniques were employed to this dataset for analysis: Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest Regression (RFR), LASSO Regression, Ridge Regression, and XGBoost Regression. Model evaluation was conducted based on two key metrics: mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and the coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). Cross-validation was conducted to ensure consistency, and the results demonstrated that Random Forest Regression and XGBoost Regression outperformed other models due to their capacity to handle non-linear, multivariate datasets. The Random Forest Regression model achieved a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 10.93%, a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.98, and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0408. The relatively inferior performance of linear models underscored the complexity of the dataset. This study demonstrates the feasibility of accurate wave energy converter (WEC) power output predictions, thereby providing valuable insights for optimising WEC systems. Future work will concentrate on optimising model performance through the application of advanced hyperparameter tuning techniques and the investigation of additional evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: Effect of Wire Size and Slot Filling Factor on the Number of Turns Per Pole in Design of SRM
abstract: As electric vehicles become increasingly important and widely used, the design of every type of electric motor has gained significant attention in both literature and industry. This study provides a detailed analysis of the number of turns in the motor windings, a critical factor in electric motor design. Through comparative analysis, it investigates how wire size and slot filling factor affect the number of windings turns per pole in Switched Reluctance Motors (SRMs). In addition, the study evaluates the effect of the number of turns analysis on motor performance during design optimization using the genetic algorithm tool in Ansys and traditional calculation methods. The optimization was performed with the wire size range between 0.45 and 0.85 mm. As a result, the optimal value with 82% efficiency was obtained with a wire size of 0.81 mm and 312 turns. The lower copper losses, ideal volume, reduced costs, and enhanced efficiency are obtained by determining the optimal number of turns. This research contributes to developing more efficient and cost-effective electric motor designs. Future research could explore various and more effective optimization techniques and current parameters to design SRM and other motors.

articleTitle: PID-F Controlled LFC in a Two-Area Power System with Renewable Integration Using Metaheuristic Approaches
abstract: As a result of the rising usage of renewable energy sources (RES) and the altering load profile, it is becoming increasingly difficult to strike a balance between production and demand. This is because renewable energy sources are becoming more prevalent. For this reason, it is of the utmost importance to put the process of load frequency control (LFC) into action. Taking this into consideration, the objective of this study is to optimize the adjustment of the parameters of the proportionalintegral-derivative with filter (PID-F) controller for the LFC process in a two-area power system that consists of photovoltaic (PV) panels and wind energy systems simultaneously. During the past few years, a number of innovative algorithms have been developed. These algorithms include the mountain gazelle optimizer (MGO), the hippopotamus optimizer (HO), and the puma optimizer (PO). The parameters of the PID-F controller were determined with the help of these algorithms, which were applied accordingly. The findings of the simulation reveal that all three algorithms managed to achieve results that were successful and comparable to one another in the LFC process. These results were attained by all three algorithms.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Energy Storage Solutions in Microgrids: A Comparison in Terms of Flexibility and Economics
abstract: The environmental damage caused by traditional energy sources such as coal, oil and natural gas, the dependence on foreign energy and the depletion of these traditional sources have increased the interest in renewable energy sources. However, renewable sources present challenges related to seasonal and geographical constraints in energy production. In response, hybrid energy systems are being developed to increase the efficiency of the use of renewable sources. Economical and reliable microgrid systems that can meet sudden load changes are required. The Hybrid Optimization Model for Electric Renewable Energy (HOMER) software facilitates hybrid optimization of various energy sources to determine the most efficient sizing. HOMER evaluates the net costs associated with various system configurations and ranks the feasible combinations. This study uses HOMER for computational simulations focusing on the pumped storage system and lithium-ion battery components for 3 MW load profiles in a proposed hybrid system. As a result, the cost, payback period and return on investment of a pumped storage system with a 3 MW load profile are much better than lithium-ion. This shows us that it is more advantageous to use pumped storage systems in large capacity systems.

articleTitle: Prediction of Electricity Production from Wind and Solar Energy by Employing Regression Models
abstract: Accurately predicting electricity production from renewable energy sources is critical for sustainable energy systems. Wind and solar energy play key roles in reducing greenhouse gas emissions and reliance on fossil fuels. However, forecasting their production is challenging due to weather variability and seasonal changes. This study employs advanced regression models to predict energy production, including Linear Regression, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, XGBoost, and Random Forest. The dataset comprises hourly wind and solar energy data from France in 2020, containing 59,807 samples. Model performance was evaluated using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and R2 metrics. Random Forest demonstrated the best performance, with an MAE of 219.30 MW, RMSE of 391.11 MW, and R2 of 0.97. XGBoost also showed strong results, achieving an MAE of 729.43 MW, RMSE of 1200.45 MW, and R2 of 0.75. These results highlight the Random Forest model's superior accuracy and reliability in capturing complex patterns. This work contributes to improving the integration of renewable energy into power grids by enhancing forecasting precision.

articleTitle: Impacts of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations on the Capacity of Distribution Transformers
abstract: In this study, some impacts of the significant paradigm shift created by increasing e-mobility applications on existing energy systems are discussed. The main purpose of the study is to examine the increasing capacity problems due to electric vehicle charging station loads on the network from the perspective of transformer loadings and to offer possible solutions. In the test environment created using the MATLAB Simulink software, DC fast charging stations were integrated into an urban medium voltage feeder that feeds consumers with different characteristics. The simulations include cases where charging stations are connected to the grid and when they are not. Analysis results show that in scenarios where charging stations are active, transformer loads increase significantly and current capacity limits are exceeded. This situation necessitates costly infrastructure improvements due to overloading of transformers, risks grid operation security and negatively affects supply continuity. To solve these problems, different consumption strategies were examined and the results were shared.

articleTitle: Prediction of Time-Delay Neural Network Modeling for First Order Control System
abstract: This study explores the use of neural networks to predict the parameters of a first-order time-delay system based on its response to a step input. A feed forward neural network architecture is proposed to estimate the gain, time constant, and time delay, which are traditionally difficult to obtain through classical methods. The model accurately estimates system parameters, with minimal deviation between the original and predicted responses. This approach offers a robust framework for parameter estimation in time-delay systems and holds potential for broader applications in system control.

articleTitle: Virtual Synchronous Generator Droop Control for Renewable Energy Sources
abstract: The connection of large-scale RES (renewable energy source) to the grid and the increase in the efficiency of energy production also causes different power quality problems. It has become mandatory for these inverter-based systems to participate in load frequency control. For this purpose, the design and simulation of a virtual synchronous generator (VSG), which enables RES to operate like synchronous generators, has been carried out in Matlab/Simulink environment. It is observed that the VSG keeps the load frequency stable according to different load conditions.

articleTitle: Simulation of the Flywheel Energy Storage System for an Industrial Robotic System
abstract: The processes performed by industrial robots should not be interrupted. Power outages are an important reason for the disruption of production processes. FESS systems are an important energy storage system that has become more current in recent years. The important advantages of this system are that it does not have a half-life and can achieve high power density in a small volume. In this study, the energy of the robot performing an industrial process was provided by FESS. In this system operating at high speeds, energy production is achieved by using the L inductance between the inverter and the motor in the generator mode. While the system was working as a generator, the inverter was switched as a boost converter thanks to this inductance. Thus, DC link voltage was obtained for the robot power system.

articleTitle: Direct Synthesis-Based Optimal PIDD2 Controller Design for Enhanced Load Frequency Control in Electrical Power Systems
abstract: The increasing load demand in power system (PS) networks necessitates the improvement of system stability and the preservation of the reliability of electrical power systems (EPS). This case is critical for ensuring energy supply security and maintaining sustainable system performance. Specifically, sudden load changes cause deviations in frequency and tie-line power values from their nominal levels in interconnected power systems (IPS), making load frequency control (LFC) an essential requirement. This research presents a Proportional-Integral-Derivative plus Second Order Derivative (PIDD<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) controller design for LFC in IPS, tuned using the Direct Synthesis Method (DSM). The design is developed for single, and two-area PS, encompassing both reheated and non-reheated thermal turbine models. In the proposed design method, controllers are designed for disturbance rejection. The controller parameters were obtained using a novel objective function that includes the settling time and Integral of Absolute Error (IAE). The results demonstrate that the proposed design surpasses the compared methods in terms of frequency and tie-line power deviations, and the robustness of the system is validated through testing under ±25% parameter variations.

articleTitle: Increasing Electric Power System Stability by Integrating Renewable Energy
abstract: Reducing carbon emissions and tackling the world's energy problems need the integration of renewable energy sources (RES) into modern power networks. With a focus on voltage stability and overall grid reliability, this study examines how the integration of renewable energy affects the stability of the electric power system. In this work, the voltage stability of the modified IEEE 13-bus test system is investigated as a case study because of DG penetrations as the load grows. In this work, MATLAB/Simulink is utilized to perform the simulations and examine the results of the utilization of photovoltaic energy sources in distribution systems. Results from case studies and simulations show that RES improves system stability and resilience to dynamic changes in supply and demand. In this paper, testing was carried out for both increased loads and network problems. The load was increased by the following percentages in buses 671 and 675 separately: 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100%. Then, the load is increased in the two buses (671 + 675) together by the previous percentages.

articleTitle: Design of a Phase Shifted Full Bridge DC-DC ZVS Converter with Analog Control
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a 600-W Phase-Shifted Full-Bridge (PSFB) DC-DC converter with analog control. Using the UCC28950 controller, the converter achieves Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS) to minimize switching losses and improve efficiency. Key components, including the transformer, output filter, and power switches, were analyzed and optimized through theoretical calculations. Simulation results confirmed stable output voltage, reduced ripple, and successful ZVS implementation, demonstrating the converter's high efficiency and suitability for demanding applications. This study offers valuable insights into PSFB converter design for high-power systems.

articleTitle: Comparison of Sensorless Control Methods for Interior Permanent Magnet Motor
abstract: This study compares the sliding mode control (SMO) and luenberger observer (LO) methods for sensorless control of interior permanent magnet (IPM) synchronous motors. In the SMO method, a low-pass filter (LPF) is used to minimize the chattering induced by the sign function, but this also introduces phase lag, impacting accuracy. On the other hand, LO eliminates the need for filters to avoid this disadvantage of SMO, but it is more challenging to model as it includes two additional parameters. Additionally, this approach enables extraction of the back electromotive force (EMF) without distortion while reducing chattering. Both SMO and LO use a normalized phase-locked loop (PLL) to accurately predict position and speed. Finally, simulations are conducted using an IPM motor, and the results compare both of the methods.

articleTitle: Effect of Volt/Var Control on Optimal Hosting Capacity of Distributed Energy Resources
abstract: Today, distributed energy resources (DERs) are being planned for grid installation or are already generating power for the grid. Since DERs capable of participating in Volt/Var control are fully functional, the impact of Volt/Var on the existing grid should be evaluated during the design phase. Therefore, the objective of this study is to investigate the impact of Volt/Var control on the hosting capacity (HC) of DERs. For this purpose, this study optimally allocates the DERs to minimize the objective function consisting of installation cost, voltage variation and losses. The algorithm of Volt/Var control of DERs is implemented in the steady state power-flow analysis in MATLAB. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with the objective function to minimize the operational cost (e.g., cost, voltage fluctuation, and loss) is combined by the NewtonRaphson method. To make the optimization more practical, the load profile at hourly intervals and the generation cost are calculated by the energy mix of the United States. As a case study, the proposed method can usefully evaluate the effect of Volt/Var control on voltage and loss by solving the HC optimization problem.

articleTitle: Fault Analysis in Power Transformers with Finite Element Analysis and Deep Learning: A Study on Flux Distributions
abstract: In this study, a 2000 kVA power transformer with34.5/0.4 kV voltage, 50 Hz frequency, and Delta-Star connection is modeled under nonlinear loading conditions using Finite Element Analysis (FEA). Various fault types (short circuit, voltage imbalance, and harmonic distortions) that may occur under operating conditions of the transformer are analyzed through FEA simulations. For each fault type and for a healthy transformer, magnetic flux distributions are obtained. These magnetic flux distributions reflect the distinctive characteristics of each fault type, illustrating points of divergence in the transformer's internal magnetic behavior. The obtained flux distribution images are used as a dataset for the automatic classification of fault types. For the classification process, deep learning-based Artificial Intelligence (AI) models, namely ResNet18, ResNet50, VGG16, GoogleNet, and MobileNetv2, are utilized. These models are distinguished by their ability to differentiate between various fault conditions based on flux distributions. Results demonstrate that faults can be predicted from flux distribution images with accuracies up to 100%. The conducted classification studies provide an effective method for the early detection of faults in power transformers, thereby enhancing system reliability. In conclusion, this study presents a comprehensive analysis of the use of AI techniques for identifying and classifying different fault conditions in power transformers based on flux distributions. This method has the potential to optimize transformer maintenance and repair processes, thereby improving the reliability of energy systems.

articleTitle: Leveraging Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) Methods Supporting Local and Global Explainability for Smart Grids
abstract: In recent decades, Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) methods have been applied in a variety of fields, from healthcare to finance, retail, energy, and many more, with remarkable improvements. However, AI-based solutions are still questionable due to concerns regarding their trustworthiness. Explainable AI (XAI) has become an emerging research field that addresses those concerns about trustworthiness, particularly for explainability and transparency. In this study, three XAI methods supporting local and global explainability, i.e. SHAP, PFI, and LIME, are utilized to investigate the key features and their impact on the model's outputs for solar photovoltaic (PV) power generation forecasting.

articleTitle: Optimizing Parking Lot Management with Mobile Energy Suppliers for Electric Vehicles
abstract: As the increment of electric vehicles (EVs) continues, efficient parking lot management emerges as a critical concern. The constraints of traditional fixed charging stations can be mitigated by leveraging the flexibility provided by mobile energy suppliers (MES). This study explores the application of MES in public parking lots to optimize energy consumption. By integrating photovoltaic (PV) resources with grid connectivity, the dependence on grid-supplied energy is significantly reduced. A mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) optimization model has been developed to minimize energy costs. The results confirm that MES offers a dynamic and cost-effective solution, improving both parking management and energy efficiency. The economic and operational effectiveness of the proposed framework is supported by practical implementation.

articleTitle: Predicting First-Order System Parameters Using Neural Networks Trained on Multiple Test Signals
abstract: Determining the parameters of First Order System, such as the system Gain (k) and the Time Constant (τ) is crusial for control system identification. Traditional parameter estimate methods are frequently dependent on the manual assessment of specific test signals, such as step, ramp, or sinusoidal inputs. However, when trained on different test signals, neural networks provide numerous key advantages that make them especially well-suited for this task. This paper describes a neural network-based method for predicting the gain (k) and time constant (τ) of a first-order system using multiple test signals. A fully connected neural network was trained to predict these characteristics using time-series data. The results reveal that the network can effectively predict system parameters, proving the viability of using deep learning approaches to solve system identification challenges.

articleTitle: Load-Frequency Control with Mountain Gazelle Optimization Algorithm for Improving Energy Quality
abstract: The rising energy demand driven by population growth, industrialization, and modern living necessitates sustainable and efficient energy management strategies. This research focuses on the load-frequency control of an islanded microgrid consisting of components such as a diesel generator, wind turbine, solar panel, energy storage system, fuel cell, electrolyzer, and electric vehicles. To ensure system stability, four controller types—PI, PID, 2-DOFPI, and 2-DOFPID are designed. The Mountain Gazelle Optimization Algorithm (MGO) is utilized to fine-tune the parameters of these controllers.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency in Agricultural Irrigation Sustainable Agriculture of the Future
abstract: Agricultural irrigation is a basic requirement for feeding the world's population, and irrigation plays an important role in improving productivity. However, the irrigation process often consumes a large amount of energy. Energy efficiency in agricultural irrigation is a fundamental component of sustainable agriculture. Studies have shown that applications have been developed to ensure energy efficiency in agricultural irrigation. However, applications are insufficient. In this study, more effective results were obtained with the cost efficiency analysis comparison method with renewable energy and technological methods. Renewable energy sources such as solar panels and wind turbines are becoming increasingly important. Additionally, with technological advances, data analytics and smart sensors are used to optimize irrigation processes and reduce the amount of water needed. This is a critical step in terms of saving energy and water, as well as environmental protection and increasing agricultural productivity. There are some parameters that affect energy efficiency in agricultural irrigation. These parameters include the depth of the well, the distance of the well to the network, the power and quality of the irrigation engine, product-soil-moisture factors. It concludes the preferred methods by making cost, quality analysis and comparison of an agricultural land that receives direct energy and an agricultural producer that invests with data analytics that uses energy with a renewable energy method. In this study, the issue of sustainable agriculture with more efficiency at less cost is discussed with technological data.

articleTitle: Mitigating Sub-Synchronous Resonance with Adaptive Phase-Dependent Switching in Static Sub Synchronous Series Compensator
abstract: Sub-synchronous resonance (SSR) is a critical challenge in power systems, particularly in series-compensated transmission lines, where interactions between electrical and mechanical components can lead to damaging oscillations. The Static Synchronous Series Compensator (SSSC), a FACTS device, has proven effective in mitigating SSR by injecting controllable series voltage to modify line impedance dynamically. However, conventional SSSC control strategies, often based on proportional-integral (PI) controllers, can exhibit limited responsiveness during transient disturbances. This paper explores the enhancement of SSSC performance through Phase-Dependent Switching (PDS), an adaptive technique that modifies switching behavior based on real-time phase conditions. Using detailed time-domain simulations, we demonstrate that the PDS-enhanced SSSC achieves faster transient response, better damping of oscillations, and improved stability margins compared to traditional methods. The results also highlight challenges such as increased switching losses and computational demands, necessitating further research into optimized algorithms and hardware solutions. These findings underscore the potential of PDS in improving SSR damping, ensuring more reliable and efficient power system operation.

articleTitle: Optimized Output Impedance for Parallel Inverters in Microgrids Utilizing ABC Algorithm and Droop Control Method
abstract: One of the highly recognized options in the efficient electrical power distribution manners of modern electrical grids involves the integration of distributed generation systems. The critical operation challenge in a microgrid is actually how to perform parallel operation for inverters that possess effective control strategies to hold stability within the system while developing appropriate power sharing. This paper describes an effective parallel inverter output impedance optimization technique based on the Artificial Bee Colony with an advanced droop control approach. In this method, power-sharing accuracy increases considerably with the minimum range of circulating currents, thus enhancing overall stability during dynamic load transitions of the system. Extensive simulation results confirm the effectiveness of optimized droop control parameters in substantially improving stable and efficient power distribution within microgrid applications.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid GGWO–Takagi Sugeno Kang Fuzzy Type 2 Based Maximum Power Point Tracking for Photovoltaic Systems Operating Under Partial Shading Conditions
abstract: In solar systems, determining the peak power point amidst variable weather conditions or disturbances poses a significant challenge for energy efficiency. In partial shade conditions, the occurrence of various peak levels in the power and voltage curves in the solar panels complicates the tracking of the maximum power point. Under these conditions, the maksimum power point often gets stuck at local maxima, hindering the ability to determine the global MPP. This paper introduces a hybrid Takagi-Sugeno-Kang type 2 fuzzy logic technique using genetic algorithms and grey wolf algorithms to regulate the photovoltaic maximum power point tracking in partial shade conditions. The suggested system has been simulated and evaluated with MATLAB/Simulink tools under circumstances of rapidly fluctuating irradiance and partial shade. Additionally, its performance is compared against the current GA and GWO algorithms in particular. It shows that the proposed GGWO-TSK Type 2 algorithm is superior to other methods with high efficiency up to 99.98%, fast conversion time and stability time under both uniform and variable irradiance conditions.

articleTitle: Adaptive Active Filter and Wavelet PWM-Based Multilevel Inverter Structure for Improved Power Systems in More Electric Aircraft
abstract: In this study, a single-phase three-level inverter design suitable for More Electric Aircraft (MEA) applications is presented. To enhance energy efficiency and improve power quality, a wavelet-based switching method (Wavelet PWMWPWM) is employed. This proposed WPWM approach for MEA power systems is compared with the bipolar and unipolar techniques of sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM), which are widely preferred in the literature, and their performances are analyzed. Considering the limitations of these commonly used inverter topologies, an adaptive active filter (AAF) structure is integrated into the system alongside the standard LC filter configuration to minimize harmonic distortion and optimize power factor. The AAF dynamically controls reactive power, working in conjunction with the LC filter to decrease harmonic distortion and improve the power factor. This innovative combination meets the highperformance and reliability requirements of MEA applications, optimizing the efficiency of the power conversion system. The results obtained in this study demonstrate that the proposed inverter design offers significant advantages in terms of energy efficiency and power quality in MEA systems, exhibiting superior performance compared to conventional inverter designs.

articleTitle: Improving the Performance of an Incremental Conductance MPPT Algorithm Using Harris-Hawks Optimization in Photovoltaic Systems
abstract: Renewable energy's rising demand has driven significant research into optimizing photovoltaic (PV) systems, with Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithms being crucial for maximizing energy extraction under varying conditions. The widely-used Incremental Conductance (INC) algorithm performs well in steady-state conditions but faces challenges like slow convergence and inefficiency during rapid irradiance changes. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a hybrid MPPT algorithm combining the INC method with Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO), a bio-inspired meta-heuristic that mimics the hunting behavior of Harris hawks. The HHO algorithm excels in balancing exploration and exploitation, making it effective in optimizing dynamic systems and avoiding local minima. By integrating HHO with INC, the hybrid approach dynamically adjusts key parameters, such as step size and convergence criteria, to track the global Maximum Power Point (MPP) more efficiently, especially rapidly changing conditions. The adaptive capabilities of HHO improve the accuracy and speed of the INC algorithm, reducing power losses and enhancing system robustness. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the hybrid HHO-INC algorithm significantly outperforms the traditional INC approach. It achieves faster convergence to the MPP, reduces the time spent in suboptimal regions, and shows higher tracking efficiency under fluctuating conditions. Moreover, the hybrid algorithm adapts quickly to environmental changes without requiring manual intervention or parameter tuning. This research highlights the potential of hybrid MPPT algorithms to enhance the performance and reliability of renewable energy systems, offering a scalable solution for improving energy efficiency in complex, dynamic PV environments.

articleTitle: Design Selection Criteria of Single Phase Induction Machine
abstract: This paper examines how important design factors, particularly capacitance values and stator and rotor slot dimensions, affect the performance of single-phase induction motors (SPIMs). Results indicate that while increasing stator slot width decreases starting current, it also decreases efficiency and torque Similarly, larger rotor slots increase starting current while reducing starting torque and efficiency. Although it increases capacitor losses, adjusting capacitance improves efficiency, power factor, and starting torque. In order to balance efficiency and performance, ideal ranges for capacitance and slot size are proposed, offering guidance for better SPIM design.

articleTitle: An Overview of Planning for Vehicle-to-Grid Systems with Large-Scale Adoption of Electric Vehicles
abstract: The rapid adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs) has the potential to transform energy infrastructure worldwide. Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) systems, which enable bidirectional energy flow between EVs and power grids, offer a promising solution for balancing electricity demand, supporting renewable energy integration, and enhancing the resilience of power grids. This paper explores different strategic planning considerations necessary for the large-scale adoption of V2G-enabled EVs, aiming to support a more resilient and sustainable energy infrastructure.

articleTitle: Arc Flash Analysis Review at Various Applications and Voltage Levels of Power Systems
abstract: When electrical failure impact can threat human life, it is worthy look closer and move always with upfront preparation and precautions to prevent falling in such a too high-cost results, This paper aims to be a good starting point for researchers who are closely looking at arc flash, high impact electrical failure. It can help researchers who are willing to contribute to achieving and implementing more accurate arc flash modeling and calculations. That applies for any level of electrical power system and grid starting from generation up to end consumers by reviewing previous studies and research completed up to this study date in a way can guide researchers to gaps they can focus on especially when it comes to a large structure or system as power system, where we have generation, transmission, distribution and consuming stages. Besides the reality of having various power system topologies, valid standards ie. IEC vs. ANSI and work conditions like difference between hydro-electric power plant and photovoltaic power plant. Study is aiming to come with suggestions and may be with route correction linked to commonly used equations and methods besides trying to suggest additional factor ie. weather temperature affect, humidity etc.., for higher accuracy modeling.

articleTitle: Systems of Smart Load Management for More Electrical Aircraft
abstract: In recent years, More Electric Aircraft (MEA) concepts have garnered significant attention due to their potential to enhance efficiency and reduce emissions in the aviation industry. However, this transition has also introduced significant challenges in power management. With the replacement of traditional hydraulic and pneumatic systems by electric systems, the management of electrical loads has become more complex. The need for smart load management is crucial to ensure uninterrupted power to critical systems while optimizing energy efficiency and enhancing system reliability. This paper presents an innovative smart load management system designed to improve the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of MEA power distribution networks. The proposed system is equipped with sensors for continuous monitoring of voltage, current, and power, integrating a battery, generators, loads, switches, and relays. It incorporates advanced control mechanisms such as real-time load prioritization and dynamic reconfiguration. The system ensures the continuous and optimal distribution of loads, monitors the health status of generators, and transfers loads to backup power sources when necessary to maintain system stability. Simulation results demonstrate that the system outperforms traditional load management techniques in terms of power utilization, response time, and overall system stability. These results validate the potential of smart load management systems to support the scalability and sustainability of MEA architectures, providing a roadmap for future advancements in aviation electrification.

articleTitle: A Cost-Effective 3D Finite Element Model for Predicting Transient Heat Transfer in U-tube Ground Heat Exchangers
abstract: Ground Source Heat Pumps (GSHPs) offer an energy-efficient and eco-friendly alternative to conventional heating and cooling systems by utilizing stable ground temperatures. This study presents a cost-effective and computationally efficient three-dimensional Finite Element Model (FEM) in COMSOL Multiphysics for predicting outlet temperatures and heat transfer rates in U-tube Ground Heat Exchangers (GHE), crucial for evaluating GSHP performance. The model examines three boundary condition scenarios: (1) uniform initial ground temperatures with constant surface temperature, (2) a Kasuda-based non-uniform profile, assuming constant average soil thermal properties, and (3) time- and depth-varying ground and surface temperatures from experimental data at Peniel Farm, Lexington, VA, with AI-based soil property predictions. Validated against reported laboratory data, the model accurately captures transient behaviors for both constant and interrupted heat inputs. By employing a detailed grid generation methodology, our approach achieves high accuracy with minimal computational costs, establishing the basic COMSOL package as a practical alternative to expensive Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) models. Results show that while constant temperature assumptions have minimal impact on outlet temperatures, heat transfer rates vary significantly near the borehole surface, emphasizing the importance of realistic boundary conditions in GHE simulations.

articleTitle: Frequency Stability Improvement of Integrated Micro-Grid Using Battery Storage System Based Distribution Static Compensator (BESS-DSTATCOM)
abstract: Dynamic instability challenges can be encountered in microgrids (MG), especially frequency fluctuations generated at the point of common coupling (PCC), leading to an unreliable microgrid. A novel method of improving frequency stability of the wind based microgrid is proposed in this study through the integration of a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) with a Distribution Static Compensator (DSTATCOM). A BESS- DSTATCOM with a six pulse regulated control scheme that manages reactive power while mitigating frequency instabilities, especially in fault event scenarios becomes part of the system. Prolonged frequency disturbances at the PCC due to faults are critical to MG stability and need to be addressed for reliable MG operation. Through the proposed BESS DSTATCOM approach, reactive power management is optimized to maintain system frequency as consistent as possible. The proposed method was developed, tested, and verified in MATLAB, showing that this approach successfully improves frequency stability in the microgrid under various operating conditions. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the BESS DSTATCOM strategy on MG operation.

articleTitle: A Sustainable Dispositional and Situational Security Awareness Model for Smart Grids
abstract: The continuous introduction of emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) in smart grids has improved the reliability of operations and communication among components in the grids. However, such technologies can become unsustainable and further introduce security vulnerabilities. Any potential impact of security attacks on a smart grid component such as a sensor, either through internal or external adversaries, may lead to a breakdown of operations in the grids. Additionally, the large number of components along with their dependencies on emerging technologies may hinder the ability of grid operators to sustainably identify security flaws. Note that sustainability (of smart grid security) in this work refers to the ability to mitigate security vulnerabilities or attacks without overdependence on grid operators or emerging technologies that introduce high computational overheads. In this paper, we propose a sustainable dispositional and situational security awareness model through the utilization of a Fuzzy Cognitive Map (FCM) to effectively reveal and mitigate security vulnerabilities in the smart grids without overdependence on emerging technologies. We conducted some case studies on a Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system to show the usefulness of our model.

articleTitle: Analog FOPID Controller Design for a Non-Ideal DC-DC Buck Converter Using a Novel Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to analog controller design for non-ideal DC-DC buck converters using an enhanced version of the Cooperation Search Algorithm (CSA). The proposed algorithm, called OCSANM, integrates Opposition-Based Learning (OBL) and the Nelder-Mead (NM) algorithm to overcome the limitations of traditional evolutionary algorithms. The OCSANM algorithm is used to optimize the parameters of a Fractional Order Proportional Integral Derivative (FOPID) controller, considering disturbance rejection effects and crossover frequency constraints. The implementation includes a comprehensive analog circuit design using operational amplifiers. Simulation results demonstrate that the OCSANM-FOPID controlled system achieves superior performance compared to both the conventional CSA algorithm and traditional pole placement method. Specifically, the proposed approach shows enhanced stability characteristics, improved disturbance rejection capabilities, and better transient response characteristics. These results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method for practical power electronics applications.

articleTitle: Design of a Prototype Dynamic Line Rating System for Real-Time Monitoring of Overhead Transmission Lines
abstract: Demand and consumption for electrical energy are continuously increasing. To meet this demand, new energy sources are being harnessed, and the capacities of existing production facilities are being enhanced. Despite supply chain challenges, construction delays, and high raw material prices, between 500 and 550 GW of new renewable energy capacity was achieved globally in 2024. It is projected that renewable energy will account for nearly 95% of the expansion in global power capacity by 2026. The increase in the number of renewable power plants daily forces the current carrying capacity of the transmission lines to be sized and installed. Dynamic Line Rating (DLR) systems allow real-time monitoring and rating of a transmission line's conductor deflection, surface temperature, ambient temperature, and weather data. These systems enable the capacity of the existing transmission lines to be at the maximum level, integrate solar and wind energy into these lines without the need for new infrastructure installations, and minimize the fault detection and maintenance-repair processes. In this study, a prototype DLR system, encompassing both hardware and software, has been designed. The prototype has been tested in a laboratory environment on a Sparrow 2AWG ACSR conductor and remotely monitored in real-time. This design calculates the ampacity according to the IEEE 738–2012 Std. methodology by measuring the weather conditions and conductor temperature values with sensors.

articleTitle: Smart Meter Analytics for Residential Energy Efficiency
abstract: Smart meters, in addition to measuring users' energy consumption, provide high-resolution, real-time energy usage data, enabling advanced analyses to uncover patterns, detect anomalies, and optimize residential energy usage. This study analyzes data representing one-hour segments of voltage and current waveforms collected over 96 days from a single-family household in Portugal. The data was converted into MP3 format for analysis and processed using the MATLAB© software package to extract hourly energy consumption metrics, including active power, reactive power, and RMS values, scaled to megawatt-hours (MWh). The conducted analyses included fundamental evaluations and anomaly detection. Statistical analysis revealed consistent consumption patterns tightly concentrated within a narrow range (75.10–75.90 MWh). The average energy consumption across the datasets was approximately 75.5 MWh, with a low standard deviation (∼0.2 MWh), indicating stable usage trends. While timeseries graphs effectively visualized these patterns and deviations, histograms provided limited insights due to the narrow data distribution. This study demonstrates the potential of smart meter data for identifying inefficiencies and enabling data-driven energy management strategies. The methodology supports advanced analyses such as load profiling, anomaly detection, and consumption optimization, showcasing scalability and applicability to larger datasets. Additionally, this research contributes to identifying hidden usage patterns and advancing smart meter methodologies.

articleTitle: Forecasting Wind Energy Production: Analysis of Meteorological and Temporal Variables Using Optimized Regression Modeling
abstract: In order to meet the power demand in energy generation systems, it is of great importance to predict the production potential in advance. In energy systems such as wind energy, whose generation potential is directly dependent on atmospheric conditions, it is possible to make short or medium-term forecasts based on meteorological data. In addition, the safe operation, efficient planning, operation, and control of wind turbines are also facilitated by predictability. The proposed study aims to improve the accuracy of wind energy forecasts through regression models supported by an optimization algorithm. In the proposed study, the potential energy production of a wind turbine is modeled using genetic algorithm-optimized artificial neural networks (GA-ANN) and gradient boosting (GA-GB) techniques. In the proposed study, one year of energy production data for Nordex N117/3600 model wind turbines is used in combination with NASA's hourly meteorological conditions data for the same period. The success of the applied techniques is analyzed in terms of performance metrics. The R2=0.971 value of the GA-GB model shows the superiority of the model over both the ANN considered in the proposed study and the deep learning methods performed with the same dataset in the existing studies.

articleTitle: Mitigation of FIDVR Using Solid State Transformer in Active Distribution Systems
abstract: The prevalent problem of delayed voltage recovery caused by fault (FIDVR), which leads to extended power restoration after faults and possibly cascading failures, affects the transmission and distribution systems. The FIDVR issue is exacerbated by the growing utilization of air conditioning (A/C) and the significant prevalence of induction motors. A novel approach for improving the (FIDVR) in active distribution networks (ADNs) through the optimized operation of solid-state transformers (SSTs) is presented in this paper. The suggested control strategy employs the untapped potential of SSTs to manage or regulate voltage within ADNs. This method allows SSTs to actively contribute to voltage regulation by managing reactive and active power. To validate the efficiency of this work, the IEEE 13-bus system, including both static and dynamic loads, is implemented using MATLAB/Simulink. The results demonstrate that SSTs can effectively mitigate FIDVR issues, enhancing the resilience and reliability of modern power systems, particularly under conditions of high reactive power absorption.

articleTitle: Investigation of Machine Learning for Predicting the Output of Photovoltaic Solar Power
abstract: The production of solar energy is becoming a more significant part of the world's energy structure, yet its fluctuation poses special problems for grid integration and energy management. For the purpose of providing a dependable and effective power supply, accurate forecasting of solar power output is essential. This article offers a thorough method for predicting solar power output using machine learning techniques. To create forecast models, our methodology combines historical meteorological data with information on solar power generation. To capture the intricate relationships in the data, we use a variety of machine learning algorithms, such as neural networks, support vector machines, and fuzzy logic. To improve model performance, feature engineering and data preprocessing methods are used. The results of this study have important ramifications for the renewable energy sector, grid operators, and decisionmakers, providing a strategy to maximize solar energy and lessen reliance on fossil fuels.

articleTitle: An Improved Red Kite Optimization Algorithm for Designing Automatic Voltage Regulator Systems
abstract: This paper introduces LOROATS (Lemur-Optimized Red Kite Optimization with Tabu Search), a novel hybrid optimization algorithm for tuning PIDD<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> controllers in Automatic Voltage Regulator (AVR) systems. LOROATS combines the Red Kite Optimization (ROA) algorithm with Lemurs Optimization (LO) and Tabu Search (TS) to enhance exploration and exploitation capabilities while avoiding premature convergence. The algorithm was evaluated using the Zwe-Lee Gaing (ZLG) objective function, which considers multiple performance metrics. Comparative analysis with state-of-the-art optimization methods demonstrated LOROATS's superior performance in optimizing PIDD<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> controller parameters. The LOROATS-tuned AVR system achieved better transient response characteristics with zero overshoot, faster rise time, and reduced settling time. Additionally, frequency response analysis showed improved bandwidth, indicating enhanced stability and disturbance rejection capabilities. These results establish LOROATS as an effective optimization approach for AVR system control, particularly suitable for modern power systems with increasing complexity and renewable energy integration.

articleTitle: Model-Based Analysis of Factors Influencing Solar Energy Efficiency: Dust Accumulation and Shading Effect
abstract: Solar energy is widely regarded as the most significant renewable energy source, with photovoltaic (PV) cells serving as the primary component for electricity generation from solar radiation. Several factors influence the energy production efficiency of PV cells, including but not limited to, radiation levels, temperature, cable losses, dust accumulation, and shading. These factors are often interrelated, where one factor can exacerbate the impact of another. In this study, various parameters affecting solar efficiency were examined by integrating them into a model, with each factor analyzed individually. Real system data was collected, and the impact of dust accumulation on the panels was assessed by measuring its contribution to shading, which in turn reduces the amount of radiation absorbed by the photovoltaic cells. The study anticipates that similar outcomes will be observed in large-scale applications, which could play a crucial role in shaping future investment decisions. It is suggested that optimizing the tilt angle of the panels and ensuring regular rainfall can effectively reduce dust accumulation, thereby enhancing the overall system efficiency.

articleTitle: Wind Turbine Fault Detection and Prediction Using Machine Learning Methods and SCADA Data
abstract: Condition monitoring and fault detection are critical aspects of wind farm management. With the rising number and capacity of wind farms, the need for effective wind farm maintenance strategies has gained even more importance. This paper presents an approach to detect, isolate and predict wind turbine faults using machine learning methods. Data collected from the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system, a built-in feature in most wind turbines, was used. Therefore, additional hardware costs are not required, which is a major advantage. However, SCADA systems initially were not developed for fault detection aims, resulting in imperfections in data quality. Artificial Neural Networks were used to mitigate these disadvantages and successfully interpret non-linear relations. The faults targeted in this research are non-fatal but frequent faults which reduce overall performance but do not show strong indications like catastrophic faults do. This makes their prediction from SCADA data more challenging. 5 out of 7 generator heating faults were successfully predicted as early as 56 hours in advance. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach is very powerful and significantly improve current results in this field.

articleTitle: Integrating Artificial Neural Networks for Predictive Life Cycle Assessment of Electric Vehicles in Sustainable Transportation
abstract: Sustainable transportation plays a critical role in combating climate change, with electric vehicles (EVs) offering a significant solution to reducing greenhouse gas emissions. This study integrates Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) to evaluate and predict the environmental impacts of EVs under various scenarios. While LCA provides a static analysis covering production, usage, and recycling phases, the ANN model overcomes the limitations of traditional methods by delivering dynamic scenario-based predictions. According to the analysis, increasing the renewable energy share in the electricity grid from 30% to 70% can reduce usage-phase emissions by approximately 17%, as listed in Table 2. Additionally, increasing battery recycling rates from 10% to 80% reduces life cycle emissions by up to 20%, emphasizing the importance of recycling technologies. Validated against LCA data, the ANN model demonstrated a 95% accuracy rate in reliably predicting environmental impacts under different conditions. This integrated approach highlights the critical role of energy policies and technological innovations in optimizing EV sustainability. By combining LCA's analytical precision with ANN's predictive capabilities, the framework is shown to be applicable for advancing renewable energy integration, enhancing recycling infrastructure, and developing sustainable production processes. The analysis reveals a strong alignment between LCA and ANN results, emphasizing their consistency and robustness in addressing environmental impacts. Keywords—life cycle assessment, artificial neural networks, electric vehicles, sustainable transportation, renewable energy, environmental impact analysis.

articleTitle: Comparative Assessment of the Patterns of Solar Irradiance from Multiple Locations Using Deep Learning Methods
abstract: Accurate forecasting is critical in mitigating the negative effects of intermittent solar radiation when producing stable electricity from photovoltaic panels at a solar plant. Recently, artificial intelligence-based algorithms to predict solar radiation have dramatically improved solar power production efficiency. Predicting solar radiation with any degree of certainty depends on a number of variables, including the model trained with the data, the location of the data collection, the time horizon for data collection, and the quality of the training data. Solar radiation projections based on data obtained from a single place at specific time intervals predominate in the existing literature. The effect of data collection sites on model accuracy has been disregarded in this practice. Some locations are more susceptible to lower solar radiation and a more frequent cycle of intermittent solar radiation than others. As a result, gathering training data from multiple locations is required to determine the best location for establishing a solar power farm. Historical weather data from Cape Town, Durban, Limpopo, and Johannesburg were used in this study to forecast solar irradiance at 10-minute intervals. Based on the results of the experiments in this study, Limpopo is regarded as the best location for establishing a solar plant. In Limpopo, the MLP model had the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 18.87. This was the best result from the study and is considered to be above expectations. The RF model produced an RMSE value of 22.51 in Cape Town, the second-best location. Limpopo > Cape Town > Durban > Johannesburg is the order of performance. In these cities, the MLP model produced an RMSE of 18.87 with Limpopo data, the RF model produced an RMSE of 22.51 with Cape Town data, the MLP produced the lowest RMSE of 23.52 with Durban training data, and the ConvLSTM produced an RMSE of 24.85 with Johannesburg training data.

articleTitle: PV Systems Generation Prediction Considering Cloud Cover Using Deep Learning Techniques
abstract: Numerous environmental elements, including sun irradiation, temperature, shade, wind speed, and others, can significantly influence the output of photovoltaic (PV) systems. Solar generation forecasts across various time ranges are required to meet demand and grid restrictions. Short-term predictions are essential for energy trading, real-time control, and grid balancing. This paper presents a concise overview of shading due to cloud cover on the generation of PV systems. Further-more, the convolutional neural network (CNN) deep learning model predicts PV generation by considering cloud movement over a specific area. The results demonstrate that cloud cover significantly impacts the generation of PV systems. Consequently, PV power generation forecasting is essential for enhancing the stability, quality, and reliability of smart grids and modern power systems. The suggested deep learning model occupies 12% of the memory size of the state-of-the-art model. The suggested model surpasses these models in the MSE, RMSE, and MAE test set metrics, yielding values of 1 KW, 2.37 KW, and 1.35 KW, respectively.

articleTitle: Automatic Overload Detection System Application in Induction Motors with Deep Convolution Neural Networks
abstract: In induction motors (IM) fed by a sinusoidal PWM (SPWM) inverter, the sudden load current increases at different inverter switching frequencies, and different stator coil pitches differ characteristically. Being able to predict these differences is very important for rotary electrical machine designers. In this study, for an automatic overload detection system, the detection of different load levels of three-phase cage IM fed by PWM inverter, depending on the operating conditions of the IM, using the deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) method was performed. The designed DCNN automatic overload prediction model has been trained with the data set obtained by experimental applications and its reliability has been increased by testing with the five-fold cross-validation method. In the study, it was concluded that in addition to the 96% accuracy achieved with test data, DCNN overload prediction models can be used very effectively in the design of rotary electrical machines.

articleTitle: Integration of Sustainable Energy Sources Into Data Centre Electrical Systems
abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources into data center electrical systems presents a viable solution to mitigate high energy consumption and carbon emissions associated with data centers, especially in emerging markets like Ireland. This study analyzes a data center project in Dublin, Ireland, focusing on the cost-effectiveness and environmental impact of integrating solar PV and wind energy using the HOMER software platform. Real-time energy consumption and generation data were collected and processed, and weather inputs were derived from reliable sources such as ASHRAE and Met Éireann, enabling accurate load modeling and resource forecasting through ARIMA. Three system architectures were evaluated: a grid-connected base case, a grid-connected renewable system (winning case), and an off-grid renewable system. The winning case, comprising grid, PV, wind turbine, and battery storage, demonstrated a significant reduction in levelized cost of energy (LCOE) from 0.233 €/kWh to 0.04193 €/kWh and a reduction in net present cost (NPC) by 71%. Carbon emissions were reduced from 50,529,358 kg/year to 172,129 kg/year. Sensitivity analysis on wind speed and solar GHI revealed further optimizations; increasing wind speed annual average by 10% lowered the LCOE to 0.008776 €/kWh with a carbon offset equivalent to negative emissions. These findings underscore the economic and environmental viability of renewable integration in data centers, offering a scalable model to reduce operational costs and emissions in power-intensive sectors.

articleTitle: Advanced Load Flow & Fault Analysis of Renewable Energy Integration in IEEE 9 Bus Power System
abstract: Renewable energy, particularly wind & solar power, plays a crucial role in modern electric power systems due to their environmental benefits, such as reduced carbon emission and air pollution, cost-effectiveness, and potential for expanding energy access. This research focuses on analyzing the load flow analysis, fault analysis, and economic load dispatch of renewable energy integration in different scenarios within an IEEE 9 Bus power system. A fixed-speed wind turbine and a solar PV model are designed and simulated in MATLAB Simulink. We collected data to create a model of the IEEE 9 Bus system in PowerWorld Simulator to add wind and solar energy data to analyze how the system operates load flow under different conditions. Five scenarios were tested to see how the grid performs when various combinations of grid generators, wind, and solar farms are used. The optimization connects ordinary and renewable generators, with the cost function balanced to reflect the zero-fuel cost of renewable sources. Successfully find the most dependable and economic scenario for the best use of all available energy sources, along with wind, solar, and the grid generator, to ensure the system runs efficiently. The power supply stays stable, and the grid generator does not have to work as challenging, which helps optimize renewable energy utilization and offers the most excellent mix of energy sources for cost-effective, clean, and sustainable power generation.

articleTitle: Scenario-Based Insights Into GCC's Net-Zero Transition: Balancing Economic Growth with Carbon Management
abstract: The GCC region, significantly dependent on hydrocarbon exports, confronts pressing problems stemming from global transitions to net-zero emissions, jeopardizing economic stability and necessitating revolutionary energy and fiscal plans. This paper analyses three scenarios—Business-as-Usual, Renewable Transition, and Carbon Management—to assess their effects on the GCC's GDP growth, fiscal balance, oil revenues, and carbon emissions from 2025 to 2050. The findings indicate that a deliberate combination of renewable energy investments, carbon capture technologies, and international partnerships produces the most equitable benefits, fostering economic growth while minimizing emissions.

Author Keywords: carbon capture and storage fiscal diversification

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of NGFWs for Cyber-Physical System Security After the CrowdStrike Incident
abstract: The CrowdStrike outage in 2024, underscored the urgent need for robust cybersecurity measures. This study provides a rigorous scientific analysis of ten leading Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFWs) through a multi-faceted methodology. Data were collected from updated vendor datasheets, comprehensive interviews with 50 IT experts, and performance testing using live product demos. The study includes firewalls from Check Point, Cisco, Juniper Networks, Palo Alto Networks, pfSense, Sophos, Trend Micro, Forcepoint, Huawei, and SonicWall. Key performance metrics analyzed include throughput, latency, concurrent connections, and VPN capabilities. The findings reveal that Check Point and Juniper Networks SRX series lead in throughput, achieving up to 500 Gbps and 365 Gbps, respectively. Palo Alto Networks and Trend Micro excel in advanced features like AI support, scoring 10/10 in user-friendly interfaces and threat intelligence. The survey of IT experts indicated that 80% of users are satisfied with their current NGFW, but 20% expressed interest in switching to alternatives like Palo Alto Networks or Fortinet for better AI support and scalability. This paper significantly contributes to the scientific community by offering validated, comprehensive insights into NGFW performance, aiding informed decision-making in enhancing cybersecurity infrastructure post-CrowdStrike outage.

articleTitle: Region-Specific Solar Performance Estimation: The Role of Data Acquisition Systems
abstract: Accurate estimation of photovoltaic (PV) panel power output requires a reliable and comprehensive data acquisition system. This study reviews existing renewable energy measurement systems and introduces a system implemented at Afyon Kocatepe University.
